content: 1. Metronidazole Dosage and Administration: For maintenance therapy, administer 5 mg/kg intravenously over 30–60 minutes at 6 and 12 hours after the initial dose. Discontinue within 12 hours post-surgery. For oral administration, prescribe 250 mg every 8 hours for 7 days or 2 g as a single daily dose. Alternatively, 1 g orally every 12 hours for 2 doses may be used. For acute intestinal amebiasis (acute amebic dysentery), administer 750 mg orally three times daily for 5–10 days. For amebic liver abscess, prescribe 500–750 mg orally three times daily for 5–10 days. For immediate-release formulations, administer 500 mg orally every 12 hours. For extended-release formulations, prescribe 750 mg orally once daily for 7 days, taken on an empty stomach. In combination therapy for certain infections, administer 250–500 mg orally four times daily with tetracycline (500 mg) and bismuth subsalicylate (525 mg) for 14 days. 2. Drug-Resistant Bacteria: To reduce the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of antibacterial drugs, metronidazole should only be used to treat or prevent infections proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide therapy selection or modification. In the absence of such data, local epidemiology and susceptibility patterns may assist in selecting empiric therapy. 3. Drug Interactions: Dronabinol: Metronidazole increases dronabinol toxicity by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. This combination is contraindicated. Discontinue metronidazole at least 14 days before starting dronabinol. Flibanserin: Metronidazole increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. Lomitapide: Metronidazole increases lomitapide levels significantly by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lonafarnib: Metronidazole increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Avapritinib: Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the starting dose of avapritinib. Axitinib: Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is necessary, monitor closely and adjust the dose as needed. BCG Vaccine (Live): Metronidazole decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. Bosutinib: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased bosutinib levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Cholera Vaccine: Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. Cobicistat: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased cobicistat levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Dihydroergotamine: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased dihydroergotamine levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Disulfiram: Disulfiram increases metronidazole toxicity by decreasing its metabolism, leading to enhanced CNS and cardiac toxicity. This combination is contraindicated. Dronedarone: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased dronedarone levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Elacestrant: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased elacestrant levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Eliglustat: Avoid or use an alternative drug. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Reduce the dose in extensive metabolizers. Entrectinib: Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, adjust the dose of entrectinib. Ergotamine: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased ergotamine levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased erythromycin levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Everolimus: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased everolimus levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Fentanyl (Intranasal, Transdermal, Transmucosal): Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. Ivabradine: Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lemborexant: Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lovastatin: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased lovastatin levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Lurbinectedin: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased lurbinectedin levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Midazolam (Intranasal): Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors increases midazolam systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. Naloxegol: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased naloxegol levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Neratinib: Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Nirogacestat: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased nirogacestat levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Olaparib: Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose. Omaveloxolone: Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose and monitor for adverse effects. Pacritinib: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased pacritinib levels caused by CYP2E1 inhibition. Pexidartinib: Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose. Pimozide: Metronidazole increases pimozide levels by decreasing its metabolism, leading to a risk of QT interval prolongation. This combination is contraindicated. Propylene Glycol: Metronidazole may cause a disulfiram-like reaction when coadministered with propylene glycol. This combination is contraindicated. Ranolazine: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased ranolazine levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Repotrectinib: Avoid or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors before initiating repotrectinib. Selinexor: Avoid or use an alternative drug. Patients treated with selinexor may experience neurological toxicities. Avoid combining with medications that cause dizziness or confusion. Selumetinib: Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose. Silodosin: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased silodosin levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Simvastatin: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased simvastatin levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Siponimod: Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. Sirolimus: Avoid or use an alternative drug due to increased sirolimus levels caused by CYP3A4 inhibition. Tazemetostat: Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose. This detailed explanation provides a professional and comprehensive understanding of the pharmacological interactions and clinical considerations associated with metronidazole.
